page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, allocating 12 physical cores with one thread per core. It is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core performance reaches the middle 50%. Similarly, Geekbench results show a poor single-core score in the bottom 10%, but the multi-core score aligns with the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks consistently rank in the middle 50% tier, though Passmark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform poorly, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang achieve average performance.

With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads that can leverage multi-threaded execution. It is appropriate for tasks such as multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and standard database operations, as evidenced by its average Passmark database and Redis SET performance. However, due to weak single-core performance, low static web serving throughput, and poor performance on larger LLM inference tasks, it is less suitable for single-threaded applications or demanding real-time AI workloads.
